You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The diagram shows a production possibility curve for an economy that produces two goods, X and Y. good Y G F E H O good X When will the opportunity cost of producing more of good X be the largest?

options.A: moving from point E to point F
options.B: moving from point E to point G
options.C: moving from point E to point H
options.D: moving from point G to point H

questions.questionText: Which activity illustrates the consumption of a ‘free’ good?

options.A: a farmer using water taken from a river
options.B: a patient visiting a medical facility provided by a charity
options.C: a person breathing air in the countryside
options.D: a person eating their birthday cake given as a gift by a friend

questions.questionText: What is essential to eliminate scarcity?

options.A: the existence of sufficient resources to meet all needs and wants
options.B: producers consistently produce in excess of demand
options.C: the government has a surplus budget
options.D: there is equilibrium in all markets

questions.questionText: What will encourage a higher degree of division of labour?

options.A: firms wishing for a greater level of self-sufficiency
options.B: firms wishing to increase their flexibility in production
options.C: firms wishing to raise their level of productivity
options.D: firms wishing to reduce their level of risk

questions.questionText: Which business is likely to be the slowest to alter its output in response to a sustained increase in demand for its product?

options.A: a fast-food restaurant
options.B: a household cleaning service
options.C: a newspaper printer
options.D: an oil exploration company

questions.questionText: A company uses large amounts of gas to produce steel. Supplies of gas are reduced at the same time as the market for steel is hit by a recession. What can be said about the likely changes in the market for steel? equilibrium equilibrium price quantity

options.A: falls uncertain
options.B: rises uncertain
options.C: uncertain falls
options.D: uncertain rises

questions.questionText: A firm is charging a price of $12 for its product and using 80% of its production capacity of 10000 units per month. Assuming the product has unitary price elastic demand, which price should the firm charge to utilise its full capacity?

The diagram shows the demand for and supply of hotel accommodation. The market equilibrium is at point E. The hotel receives a very large number of bad reviews about the quality of its accommodation. Which point on the diagram would show the new market equilibrium? S price

options.A: B E
options.C: D D O quantity

questions.questionText: What most accurately describes a market supply curve?

options.A: supply at different income levels, assuming product prices remain unchanged
options.B: supply at different levels of factor prices, assuming product prices remain unchanged
options.C: supply at different prices, assuming no changes in technology
options.D: supply at different time periods, assuming no changes in technology

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D shows an individual’s initial demand curve for public transport. price of public transport D D O quantity of public transport What could cause the demand curve to shift to D ?

options.A: The costs of running the individual’s car fall.
options.B: The individual is no longer able to drive.
options.C: The price of public transport falls.
options.D: The public transport services are reduced.

questions.questionText: A government introduces an effective minimum price for a product but makes no other intervention in the market. This policy suggests that the government’s objective is

options.A: to discourage consumption of a demerit good.
options.B: to increase the consumption of a merit good.
options.C: to reduce the price of a private good.
options.D: to support the incomes of producers.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of an indirect tax imposed on cigarettes. The market is initially in equilibrium at point X. price S Z S P W X P e P

The diagram shows the supply curve of a product. S price ($) quantity The government imposes a specific indirect tax of $5 on the product. How will the price elasticity of supply of the product change?

options.A: from elastic (>1) to inelastic (<1)
options.B: from inelastic (<1) to elastic (>1)
options.C: from inelastic (<1) to unitary (=1)
options.D: from unitary (=1) to elastic (>1)

questions.questionText: The diagrams show a country’s aggregate demand (AD ) and aggregate supply (AS ) curves.
The diagram shows the effect on the average price level when aggregate demand (AD) increases from AD to AD .

The table lists the values of the components of an economy’s circular flow of income. component value $m government spending 6 exports 8 investment 9 imports 7 saving 10 tax 5 What can be concluded about the economy from the information shown?

options.A: It has a budget surplus.
options.B: It has a trade deficit.
options.C: It is a mixed, open economy.
options.D: Its circular flow is in equilibrium.

questions.questionText: What is a cost of negative economic growth?

options.A: deteriorating balance of payments
options.B: higher inflation
options.C: higher unemployment
options.D: increased pollution

questions.questionText: A government statistical office measured changes in income from employment, pensions and benefits, then subtracted income tax and welfare contributions and adjusted for inflation. What did the final figure represent?

options.A: changes in nominal income
options.B: changes in nominal net earnings
options.C: changes in real disposable income
options.D: changes in real gross earnings

questions.questionText: Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies is most likely to be effective in the short run to prevent deflation in a closed economy? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: decreasing the budget deficit decreasing the interest rate
options.B: decreasing the budget deficit decreasing the money supply
options.C: increasing the budget deficit decreasing the interest rate
options.D: increasing the budget deficit decreasing the money supply

questions.questionText: Which macroeconomic objective is most likely to be achieved by increasing income tax?

options.A: depreciation of the exchange rate
options.B: economic growth
options.C: low unemployment
options.D: price stability

questions.questionText: What is not a supply-side policy?

options.A: increasing government expenditure on infrastructure
options.B: increasing research and development expenditure
options.C: increasing subsidies for education and training
options.D: increasing the supply of money

questions.questionText: When can a policy be classified as macroeconomic?

options.A: when it focuses on the level of individual welfare
options.B: when it involves economy-wide institutions and behaviour
options.C: when it is based on the control of monopoly markets
options.D: when it relies on the use of buffer stock schemes

questions.questionText: The demand for a country’s exports is price elastic. If it is experiencing a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments, which combination of policies is most likely to correct the deficit? standard rate of rate of interest exchange rate income tax

options.A: decrease appreciate keep unchanged
options.B: decrease depreciate decrease
options.C: increase keep unchanged decrease
options.D: keep unchanged depreciate increase

questions.questionText: What is an unintended consequence of the US government restricting imports of cheap Chinese steel?

options.A: US importers of steel pay lower prices for steel.
options.B: US manufacturers become less competitive.
options.C: US steel makers increase steel production.
options.D: US steel workers receive higher incomes.

questions.questionText: What is an export of services in Jamaica’s current account?

options.A: an inflow of funds to Jamaica to buy shares
options.B: earnings from US tourists visiting Jamaica
options.C: earnings of Haitian workers in Jamaica sent to Haiti
options.D: the export of Jamaican coffee

questions.questionText: A country imports natural gas for which it has price-inelastic demand. What is the effect if that country imposes an import duty on the gas?

options.A: Consumers in the importing country will suffer a loss of consumer surplus.
options.B: The exporting country will gain export revenue.
options.C: The importing country’s primary income will increase.
options.D: The price of natural gas will rise in other importing countries.

questions.questionText: The table shows the output of goods X and Y in China and the United States (US) before specialisation. good X good Y China 20000 70000 US 20000 50000 total 40000 120000 Assuming both China and the US use 50% of their resources to produce each product, what will the combined total output be after specialisation has occurred?
Economists suggest that multilateral trade between many countries is preferable to bilateral trade between two countries. Why is this?

options.A: Bilateral trade means that trade diversion is always greater than trade creation.
options.B: Bilateral trade misses the benefit of trade with third countries.
options.C: Gains from bilateral trade are less than the harm done to third countries.
options.D: Gains from comparative advantage cannot apply in the case of bilateral trade.

questions.questionText: A country experiences an improvement in its terms of trade. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: a decrease in its budget deficit
options.B: a relatively low rate of domestic inflation
options.C: a rise in its exchange rate
